stem: A client with diabetes says, 'My continuous glucose monitor measures glucose directly from my blood, so I would never need a blood glucose meter.' Which response by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: A CGM sensor measures glucose in interstitial fluid and provides glucose values and trends; follow the specific device instructions for when meter confirmation or calibration is needed
options.B: A CGM measures venous blood glucose continuously through the sensor and completely replaces all other glucose testing for every device
options.C: A CGM provides only one glucose value each day and cannot display trends or alerts
options.D: CGM values are unrelated to glucose management and are used only to document exercise

rationale: FDA-cleared CGM systems use a sensor to measure glucose in interstitial fluid and can provide repeated/real-time glucose values, trends, and alerts that support diabetes management. Requirements for calibration or confirmatory fingerstick testing are device-specific, so a nurse should not teach that every CGM universally eliminates blood glucose meter use. FDA also advises meter confirmation when a sensor reading is suspected to be inaccurate or does not match symptoms. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Explain that CGMs measure interstitial glucose and provide trends/alerts, while confirmatory fingerstick or calibration requirements depend on the specific device and clinical situation.
source_document_title: Simplera System — P160007/S047; Continuous Glucose Monitoring Sensor Recall: FreeStyle Libre 3
source_version_date: FDA CGM device information current through 2026; pages accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Simplera System > How does it work?: sensor monitors glucose in interstitial fluid and transmits real-time values/trends/alerts. FreeStyle Libre 3 recall > What to Do: if symptoms do not match sensor reading or reading may be inaccurate, verify with a fingerstick blood glucose meter
source_claim_supported: CGMs measure interstitial glucose and provide ongoing values/trends/alerts; blood-glucose meter confirmation/calibration needs are device- and situation-specific rather than universally eliminated.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — monitor diagnostic data and client response, recognize inaccurate/abnormal monitoring information, and use monitoring technology safely
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — continuous glucose monitoring / safe interpretation of monitoring data
correction_summary: Corrected the blueprint from Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies to Reduction of Risk Potential. Replaced the simplistic 'real-time subcutaneous readings' statement with the technically accurate interstitial-glucose mechanism and removed the universal implication that CGM either always or never requires fingerstick confirmation.
audit_findings: A accurately states the measurement compartment and device-specific confirmation principle. B falsely says venous blood and universal replacement; C denies continuous/trend functions; D misstates the device purpose. No specific device calibration schedule is generalized to all CGMs. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
audit_reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol Rule 1 — item-by-item semantic audit
final_reaudit_scope: current FDA CGM measurement/confirmation guidance; exact device locators; A-D technology audit; zero device-generalized calibration precision; NCSBN 2026 blueprint; independent adversarial second pass
